chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ismail ibn Yasar, from Uthman ibn Affan al-Sadusi, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the bathhouse, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you want the bathhouse?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) ordered the bathhouse to be warmed, then entered and wore an izar (garment), covering his knees and navel. Then he ordered the owner of the bathhouse to anoint what was outside the izar, then said: 'Go out from me'. Then he (peace be upon him) anointed what was underneath it with his own hand, then said: 'Thus, do it'.

key_terms.طَلَى: To anoint/smear (with water or oil for purification)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to perform ritual purification when entering a bathhouse according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of maintaining ritual purity (taharah) in public spaces, specifically addressing the concern of impurity transfer from the floor of the bathhouse. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates a methodical approach where the garment is anointed externally before removal, and the body is anointed directly, ensuring that the wearer remains in a state of cleanliness for prayer. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing hygiene with the preservation of ritual validity in daily life.
